Eurovision duels — head-to-head trivia during the live show

A duel turns the dead air between performances into a battlefield. Challenge anyone in your room to a 3-question Eurovision trivia fight — the winner steals their duel score from the loser or doubles it for themselves. Two of the five end-of-night trophies (Duelist, Thief) are decided here.

What is a Eurovision duel?

A duel is a private 3-question Eurovision trivia round between exactly two players in the same room. Both players answer the same questions on a 12-second timer. The first question fires once the challenged player accepts; everyone else in the room sees a discreet "duel in progress" chip, but the questions stay private until the duel ends.

  • 3 questions. Pulled from the Eurovision trivia bank, with a fixed mix of categories.
  • 12 seconds per question. Score = 12 minus elapsed seconds, rounded down. Wrong or out of time = 0.
  • Winner takes the bigger answer total — equal totals are a tie, with no winner and no points moved. There is no flat win bonus.
  • Steal or Double. Winner picks one. Double adds twice the winner’s duel score and the loser keeps their points; Steal moves the duel score from the loser to the winner (up to what the loser has).

When duels are available

Duels open as soon as the host taps Start the Party! and stay open all through the songs, side by side with Quiz. They lock automatically at Voting Live — the moment the show’s voting opens — together with quiz and predictions, and stay locked through the results and trophy reveal. The only other time duel buttons are inactive is the Lobby, before the party starts.

Phase rule of thumb: Quiz and duels share the same window, so pace yourself: knock out your quiz rounds early, keep refining predictions as the songs play, and save duels for postcards and ad breaks — everything locks when voting opens.

Scoring math

The formula rewards speed and accuracy equally — every full second of hesitation costs you a point.

ScenarioPoints
Correct answer at 0–1 seconds11–12
Correct answer at 5 seconds7
Correct answer at 11 seconds1
Wrong / timeout0

The winner’s total earned in that duel is their duel score. There is no extra win bonus — the winner picks:

  • Steal — move your duel score from the loser’s banked total to yours. Capped at what the loser actually has (you cannot take them below zero); unavailable if they have 0 points.
  • Double — add 2 × your duel score to yourself. Loser keeps their score.

Steal vs Double — when each one wins

⚔️ Steal

Zero-sum swing — you gain your duel score and they lose it (capped at what they have). Against that one opponent the gap moves as much as with Double, so use it when the person you beat is the one you need to overtake (mid-show, leaderboard tight, you’re second by 30 points).

✨ Double

Adds twice your duel score to you — always the bigger personal gain, and the only option when the loser has 0 points. Better when you’re racing the whole room rather than this one opponent.

How duels feed the trophies

Two of the five end-of-night trophies come straight from duel data:

  • Duelist — most duels won across the night.
  • Thief — most points taken via Steal.

See the full scoring page for how Duelist and Thief feed into the Champion total, and the rule book for sudden-death tiebreaks when two players tie a trophy category.
